Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3203 : Reinforced Concrete Design { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction and design philosophy , Properties of concrete and steel reinforcement bars. Indian standard specifications and standard design Aids, design philosophy, Introduction to working stress method and Limit state method. Limit state of collapse and Limit state of serviceability. ( 4 hours)
Module 2 :

Analysis of singly and doubly reinforced rectangular sections for bending. Flanged Beams, Analysis for Shear, bond and Torsion. (10 hours)
Module 3 :

Design of beams for flexure, shear, torsion ,bond following IS 456-2000 with reinforcement detailing.(4 hours).

Module 4 :

Analysis and design of one way slab, simply supported and restrained two way slab with Reinforcement detailing. (4 hours)
Module 5 :

Types of staircases, Functional design of strair case, Design of dog-legged and Open well staircase. (4hours)
Module 6 :

Analysis and design of axially loaded short column, column subjected to uni-axial and bi-axial moments, design of slender column, Interaction curves, Design aids for reinforced concrete to IS 456. (8 hours)
Module 7 :

Analysis and design of rectangular isolated footing with axial load. (4 hours)

Course Objective

1 .

Student will learn the basic concepts of designing reinforced concrete elements
2 .

Students will learn to design beam, slab, staircase following the guidelines of IS 456-2000.
3 .

Students will learn to design short and long columns for axial, uniaxial and biaxial loadings.
4 .

Students will learn to design isolated footing.
5 .

Students will learn about reinforcement detailing in various elements.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to analyse RCC rectangular, flanged beams for bending, shear and torsion
2 .

Students will be able to design RCC beam for bending, shear and torsion following IS codes.
3 .

Students will be able to design RCC one way, two way slabs, waist slab of staircase.
4 .

Students will be able to design RCC short and long column with axial and eccentric loads

5 .

Students will be able to design RCC isolated footing for axial load.

Essential Reading

1 .

N. Subramanian, Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures, Oxford

2 .

S. Unnikrishna Pillai & D. Menon, Reinforced Concrete Design, Tata McGraw Hill, 2008

1 .

A. K. Jain, Reinforced Concrete: Limit State design, Nem Chand and Bros. 1999.

2 .

2. A. Nilson, D. Darwin, C. Dolan, Design of Concrete Structures, Tata McGraw- Hill

Journal and Conferences

B.I.S. Codes.IS 456-2000
2 .

SP -16 Design Aids for Reinforced Concrete to IS 456

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH6433 : Environmental Management System { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: Air and water pollution issues solid waste discharged, Air pollution, classification, sources, effects, Lapse Rate, Plume behavior, Numerical on stack height design, Sampling and analysis techniques: Water and air sampling methods, various analyzing techniques and recent developments in these areas. 8 hours
Module 2 :

Air pollution control devices: settling chamber, Electrostatic precipitators, cyclone separators, fabric filters. 10 hours
Module 3 :

Water pollution: Introduction, water pollutant sources, effects on human beings, animals and buildings, Water characteristics and its monitoring: physical, chemical and biological characteristics of waste water, different methods of testing, analysis and continuous monitoring., Methods for treatment of waste water: preliminary treatment, primary treatment, secondary treatment and continuous monitoring, Advanced water treatment method: adsorption, membrane separation. Numericals on waste water treatment: Activated sludge process, trickling bed filtration. 8 hours
Module 4 :

Solid waste management: Introduction, types of waste, E-waste, Industrial, radioactive wastes, Classification of solid waste and treatment: Municipal solid waste, E-waste, Industrial waste, radioactive wastes. 6 hours
Module 5 :

Environmental management system: Introduction, Objectives, EMS techniques, Environmental Impact Assessment: Introduction to EIA, evolution, EIA documentation and process, Environmental Audit: Introduction to EA, methods, waste audit and pollution prevention assessment, Life Cycle Assessment and ISO 14000 series: Goal, scope of LCA, procedures for LCA, application of LCA, Integrated System for EMS. 8 hours

Course Objective

1 .

To enable the students with basic concepts on Environmental pollution control and management
2 .

To demonstrate the students with various environment standards and help them in decision making
3 .

To learn the basic design of air pollution control devices.

Course Outcome

1 .

To understand the basic concepts on environmental issues and pollution control methods
2 .

To design the air pollution control devices.
3 .

To demonstrate the water pollution abatement techniques for various scenarios.
4 .

To categorize solids waste handling methods for proper management.
5 .

To apply various environmental management tools for different environmental related applications.

Essential Reading

1 .

S. Alan, Environmental Biotechnology, Oxford University , 2005

2 .

Christopher S. and Mark Y., Environmental Management Systems, Routledge Publications , 2006

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Howard S.Peavy, Donald R. Rowe & George Tchobanoglous, Environmental Engineering, Mc .Graw hill , 1985

2 .

K.L. Mulholland, J.A. Dye,, Pollution Prevention: Methodology, Technologies and Practices, Wiley publication , 1998

7619.t: EE6474: Power Electronics and Drives Simulation Laboratory
7619.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6474 : Power Electronics and Drives Simulation Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Simulation of various power electronics converters and their motor drives applications in the MATLAB/Simulink, dc-dc converters: Boost converter, Buck converter and Flyback converter, closed-loop voltage control mode operation of Flyback converter, dc motor drives using universal bridge PWM converter, dc motor drives using closed-loop controlled GTO based dc-dc converter, induction motor drive with constant V/f control, induction motor drive using the P-I controller, induction motor dynamic model simulation during free acceleration, simulation of three-phase PWM active rectifier acting as the utility interface for the input line current wave shaping to improve line current THD.
List of Experiments
1. Simulation of Boost converter
2. Closed loop control of Buck converter (Average current mode control)
3. Simulation of Flyback converter
4. Closed loop control of Flyback converter (Voltage mode control)
5. DC motor drive using universal bridge PWM converter
6. Closed loop control of dc motor Drives using GTO based dc-dc Converter
7. V/f control of induction motor
8. Induction motor drive using P-I controller
9. Three phase PWM rectifier for utility interface with active current shaping for unity power factor
10. Simulation of dynamic model induction motor to plot torque vrs. speed characteristics for free acceleration

Course Objective

1 .

To acquire skill in Simulink simulation of power electronic converters and dc drives
2 .

To simulate induction motor drive in Simulink using closed loop V/f control
3 .

To simulate three phase PWM rectifier for utility interface with active current shaping for unity power factor
4 .

To verify dynamic model of induction motor in reference frames through simulation using MATLAB programming

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Ability to simulate power electronic circuits in Simulink
CO2: Ability to simulate dc motor drive in Simulink
CO3: Ability to simulate V/f control of induction motor drive drives
CO4: Skill to design and simulate closed loop induction motor drive using P-I controller
CO5: Ability to simulate three phase PWM rectifier for utility interface with active current shaping for unity power factor
CO6: Ability to simulate induction motor transients through MATLAB programming

Essential Reading

1 .

M.B. Patil, V. Ramanarayanan, V.T. Ranganathan, Simulation of Power Electronic Circuits, Narosa Publishing House, New Delhi , 2009

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN3101 : Underground Metal Mining { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 01: Various types of ore body and their geological features,selection of mine access, development of drift, drive, decline, raise , ramp etc. selection of stoping methods [6 hours]
Module 02:Special underground facilities: Shaft pockets, ore pass , ore bins, ore transfer raises, sump, skip loading system, crusher house, grizzly etc.[6 Hours]
Module 03: Pillar supported stoping methods like room and pillar, cut and fill with post pillar, sublevel open stoping with barrier pillar etc.[6 hours]
Module 04: Artificially and fill supported stoping methods like shrinkage, cut and fill, Square set, VCR, sublevel with filling etc.[6 hours]
Module 05: Unsupported with caving methpods like sublevel caving, block caving etc.[6 hours]
Module 06: Stope fills: preparation, transportation and filling operation,[3 hours]
Module 07: Solution mining: in situ leaching, Mining of placer deposits, under-sea mining, [3 hours]

Course Objective

1 .

To make the students conversant with the different types of underground metal mining methods and their variants.
2 .

To make the students conversant regarding modern trackless underground metal mine planning and designing which are being operated by deploying different types of the heavy earth moving machineries like LHD, LPDT, Jumbo drill Machine etc.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: The student will understand the development procedures of various underground metal mine structures for continuous mine operation
CO2: The student will learn about different types of stope development and operation methods
CO3: The student will gain knowledge on underground metalliferous mine planning, designing and operation scheduling

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH4003 : Classical Mechanics { 3-1-0 / 4}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: (4 hours)
Review of Lagrangian formalism and its application, Hamilton’s principle and Hamiltonian mechanics.
Module 2: (14 hours)
The equation of canonical transformation, the sympletic approach to canonical transformation, infinitesimal canonical transformation, Poisson brackets and other canonical invariant, conservation theorem in Poisson bracket formulations, angular momentum Poisson bracket relations. Hamilton-Jacobi theory: Hamilton-Jacobi equation for Hamilton-principle & Hamilton's characteristic functions, separation of variables in H. J. equations, cyclic coordinates, action angle variables for one degree freedom, action angle variables for completely separable systems.
Module 3: (9 hours)
The Kinematics of rigid body motion: Co-ordinates of rigid body, Orthogonal transformation, Properties of transformation matrix, Euler angles, Euler's theorem in motion of rigid body, Infinitesimal rotations, Rate of change of vectors, Coriolis effects.
Module 4: (9 hours)
Rigid body dynamics: Angular momentum & Kinetic energy of motion about a point, inertial tensor and moment of inertia, principal axis transformation and eigenvalue values of inertia tensor, Euler equation of motion, torque free motion of rigid body, heavy symmetrical top with one point fixed, Gyroscope.
Module 5: (5 hours)
Small Oscillations: Formulation, Eigenvalue equation and principal axis transformation, Free vibration and normal coordinates, dissipation and forced vibrations.
Module 6: (7 hours)
Special theory relativity: Basic postulates of special theory of relativity, Lorenz transformation, velocity addition, Relativistic kinematics of collisions and many particle systems, Lagrangian,
Hamiltonian formulations in relativistic mechanics, illustrations (1D harmonic oscillator, hyperbolic motion of particle, motion of a charged particle), Covariant formulation Lagrangian.

Course Objective

1 .

To gain an understanding of advanced theories beyond Newtonian mechanics of dynamics of classical systems having full range of speed.
2 .

To equip students with effective research skills.
3 .

Understanding the concept of Symmetries.
4 .

To enhance skills for solving real problems in dynamics using abstract mathematical language.
5. To help students for smooth transition to theories of quantum physics.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to learn:
CO1: The fundamentals of Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics and their application in solving problems in classical dynamics.
CO2: The methods like canonical transformation and Poisson brackets to simplify the problem and to find the solutions of a system in phase space. The advanced methods of Hamiltonian-Jacobi and Action-angle variables to find the equation of motion and frequency of periodic motions respectively.
CO3: The kinematics of rigid body and its application to real physical events.
CO4 Dynamics of rigid body with their applications to real problems.
CO5: The formulation of small oscillations of objects which have plenty of applications in other branch of physics.
CO6: Glimpse of advanced special theory of relativity

Essential Reading

1 .

H. Goldstein, C. P. Poole, and J. Safko, Classical Mechanics, Pearson Education , 3rd Edition.

2 .

L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, Mechanics: Course of Theoretical Physics - Vol. 1, Elsvier , 3rd Edition.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

L. Susskind and G. Hrabovsky, Classical Mechanics: The Theoretical Minimum, Penguin Publisher (2014)

2 .

K. N. Srinivasa Rao, Classical Mechanics, Universities Press (India) Pvt Ltd.
